questions.prompt: What is the capital city of United Kingdom?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the United Kingdom article.

questions.proof: The UK's capital city and largest city is London in England.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of United Kingdom?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the United Kingdom article.

questions.proof: About 95 percent of the UK's population can only speak English.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It had the sixth largest economy in the world by nominal GDP in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the United Kingdom article.

questions.proof: It had the sixth largest economy in the world by nominal GDP in 2019.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “At its height in _____, more than 458 million people lived in the British Empire, one-fifth of the Earth's population.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the United Kingdom article.

questions.proof: At its height in 1922, more than 458 million people lived in the British Empire, one-fifth of the Earth's population.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Britain continued to be the biggest manufacturing economy in the world until _____ and the largest economy until the 1920s.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Economy” part of the United Kingdom article.

questions.proof: Britain continued to be the biggest manufacturing economy in the world until 1908 and the largest economy until the 1920s.
